description: The Oracle constellation contains three independent fourteen-node paths: Foresight · Deep Insight · Knowledge. Optional synergy notables support combinations; the all-path apex checks all three branches.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Finish each branch through its own prerequisites; a synergy node is not a shortcut to a different apex.

quests.title: Try the playstyle
description: Practice a support or recovery spell in a safe space and carry a weapon for times when mana is low.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: The activity check records your practice. It does not require you to spend points or commit to this class.
steps: Equip suitable gear you already have.
Practice in the town training yard.
Write down one strength and one weakness you noticed.

guide_chapters.title: Path of the Occultist
guide_chapters.subtitle: Class foundation · compare all three specializations

quests.title: Occultist at a glance
description: Blood, Ender and Eldritch themes with a less forgiving health foundation. Read the three specializations below, then make your personal investment in the skilltree.
quests.goal: Decide whether this combat foundation suits you.
tips: Reading this page does not select the class. Compare the root’s bonuses and penalties on the actual skill node.

quests.title: Build your foundation
description: Your five inner branches are Forbidden Study, Dark Reserve, Blood Rite, Void Study and Eldritch Study. Each branch contains four mandatory foundation nodes. Complete their requirements, class mastery and the specialization gate before entering a subclass.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Twenty inner foundation nodes are only part of the route; account for entry, root, mastery and gate nodes too.

quests.title: Blood Mage
description: More Blood-school power; lower Holy power, maximum health and melee damage. These are the subclass’s starting tradeoffs and direction, not your character’s final stat totals.
quests.goal: Understand the Blood Mage playstyle and its tradeoffs.
tips: Read health-related costs before casting. A low-health character needs a reliable recovery plan.
steps: Compare the subclass root with your other two options.
Inspect its three paths: Sanguine Power · Sacrifice · Crimson Mastery.

quests.title: Blood Mage · three paths
description: The Blood Mage constellation contains three independent fourteen-node paths: Sanguine Power · Sacrifice · Crimson Mastery. Optional synergy notables support combinations; the all-path apex checks all three branches.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.

quests.title: Necromancer
description: Supports summon damage when that attribute exists, otherwise the script uses its spell-power fallback. More mana; lower Fire, Ice and Lightning power. These are the subclass’s starting tradeoffs and direction, not your character’s final stat totals.
quests.goal: Understand the Necromancer playstyle and its tradeoffs.
tips: The tree strengthens supported summons; obtain and test the actual summon spell separately.
steps: Compare the subclass root with your other two options.
Inspect its three paths: Summoning · Grave Reserve · Lord of the Dead.
Choose and invest in the personal skilltree when you are ready.

quests.title: Voidcaller
description: More Eldritch power, Ender power and mana; lower armor, health and melee damage. These are the subclass’s starting tradeoffs and direction, not your character’s final stat totals.
quests.goal: Understand the Voidcaller playstyle and its tradeoffs.
tips: Carry a dependable escape tool and check which spells actually use your chosen school.
steps: Compare the subclass root with your other two options.
Inspect its three paths: Eldritch Power · Void Power · Abyssal Reserve.
Choose and invest in the personal skilltree when you are ready.

quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.

quests.title: Try the playstyle
description: Test your chosen spell school safely and compare recovery options before using health-trading nodes.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: The activity check records your practice. It does not require you to spend points or commit to this class.

Practice in the town training yard.

guide_chapters.title: Professions & Everyday Work
guide_chapters.subtitle: Seven profession islands · activities that support your kingdom

quests.title: Choose useful everyday strengths
description: Mining, Logging, Hunting, Exploration, Fishing, Farming and Crafting are skilltree investments alongside your combat build. You may take up to three profession masteries and up to three of the six focus nodes in each profession.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: You can still do every activity without specializing in its profession.
quests.caution: These activities do not implement a separate profession XP counter or award automatic skill points.

quests.title: Mining · profession
description: Excavation and mining speed, ore-loot duplication chance and interaction reach. Inspect the three branches and six focus options in your personal tree before committing points.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Check a loot-duplication node’s ore conditions. It is a chance, not a guaranteed double output.

quests.title: Mining · field assignment
description: Prepare a marked mining route, sort its haul and reserve material for the next workshop.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Check a loot-duplication node’s ore conditions. It is a chance, not a guaranteed double output.

quests.title: Logging · profession
description: Axe-based chopping, movement and axe durability. Inspect the three branches and six focus options in your personal tree before committing points.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: A Create saw’s output and a player’s axe-conditioned bonus are different systems.

quests.title: Logging · field assignment
description: Harvest a wood supply, save the saplings and establish a repeatable replanting area.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: A Create saw’s output and a player’s axe-conditioned bonus are different systems.

quests.title: Hunting · profession
description: Movement, mob-loot duplication chance and mob experience. Inspect the three branches and six focus options in your personal tree before committing points.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Keep a retreat route and reserve some inventory space for unexpected drops.

quests.title: Hunting · field assignment
description: Complete a planned hunting trip and bring useful mob supplies back to the storehouse.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep a retreat route and reserve some inventory space for unexpected drops.

quests.title: Exploration · profession
description: Travel speed, chest-loot duplication chance and luck. Inspect the three branches and six focus options in your personal tree before committing points.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Keep the discovery’s location even when you cannot clear the structure yet.

quests.title: Exploration · field assignment
description: Find a structure, record its location and return with a documented discovery.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep the discovery’s location even when you cannot clear the structure yet.

quests.title: Fishing · profession
description: Fishing-loot duplication chance, luck and fishing-rod durability. Inspect the three branches and six focus options in your personal tree before committing points.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Read the node and rod conditions; a fishing bonus does not guarantee a particular rare catch.

quests.title: Fishing · field assignment
description: Set up a fishing spot and stock fish for meals or recipes your team uses.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Read the node and rod conditions; a fishing bonus does not guarantee a particular rare catch.

quests.title: Farming · profession
description: Interaction reach, health support for farm work and hoe-conditioned breaking speed. Inspect the three branches and six focus options in your personal tree before committing points.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: The current profession does not give an automatic crop-growth-rate bonus.

quests.title: Farming · field assignment
description: Create crop and animal-feed reserves that remain stocked after the factory takes its share.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: The current profession does not give an automatic crop-growth-rate bonus.

quests.title: Crafting · profession
description: Repair efficiency, free-enchant chance and mining-equipment durability. Inspect the three branches and six focus options in your personal tree before committing points.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Crafting profession nodes do not remove recipe ingredients or provide free mechanisms.

quests.title: Crafting · field assignment
description: Prepare a repair and equipment station, then maintain tools used by the workshop and explorers.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Crafting profession nodes do not remove recipe ingredients or provide free mechanisms.

guide_chapters.title: Combat, Movement & Equipment
guide_chapters.subtitle: Practice first · Epic Fight, ParCool, weapons and accessories

quests.title: Build a loadout you can use
description: The selected pack combines Epic Fight, Weapons of Miracles, Simply Swords, Iron’s spells, movement tools and the personal skilltree. Read the controls and test one complete loadout before taking it into a boss arena.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Change one equipment piece at a time when comparing builds.

quests.title: Use the training yard
description: Use a safe target to compare attacks, recovery, mana cost and movement. A dummy can help with controlled comparisons, but a stationary target does not reproduce a boss’s movement or resistance.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Repeat the same short attack sequence with both loadouts.

quests.title: Learn your weapon moves
description: Epic Fight and its weapon addons can give different weapons distinct attacks. Check battle-mode controls and the actual weapon’s supported moves rather than assuming every weapon handles alike.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Reserve room around the target while learning an unfamiliar combo.

quests.title: Practice a clean escape
description: ParCool adds movement options with their own controls and conditions. Practice on a safe course, check your available movement resources and learn a route back to solid ground.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Test ladders, ledges and recovery in town before attempting the same movement over a dangerous drop.

quests.title: Armor and tradeoffs
description: Compare armor, durability, affixes and effects with your class penalties. A damage-focused subclass may give up health or armor; a casting build may need mana or regeneration as much as raw attack damage.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Do not discard a useful lower-rarity item merely because the replacement has a brighter name.

quests.title: Curios, Artifacts and Relics
description: Artifacts, Relics and their selected integrations add equipment with their own activation and upgrade rules. Read their tooltips and inspect Curios slots. Carry a few useful effects instead of assuming every found item works from the main inventory.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Test the effect in a safe area and check any charge, cooldown or unlock condition.

quests.title: Growing a relic
description: Reliquified Artifacts, Ars Nouveau and Twilight Forest extend the corresponding equipment systems. Follow the actual relic’s progression screen and requirements; an item discovery and a fully developed relic are different goals.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Build around a relic you can use regularly, and note which activities advance its own requirements.

quests.title: Affixes, gems and enchanting
description: Apotheosis and the selected Apothic systems add equipment and enchanting layers. Inspect affixes, sockets and the relevant workstation recipes in JEI before modifying a favorite item.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Use spare equipment to learn a workstation’s behavior before committing your best gear.

quests.title: Prepare a recovery kit
description: Keep spare food, tools, blocks and a return plan at home. Shared quest progress does not remove the need to recover from an expedition that goes wrong.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Make the kit accessible to teammates who may help you return.

guide_chapters.title: Automation Workshop
guide_chapters.subtitle: Materials → mechanism → casing → machine · build reliable supply lines

quests.title: A factory starts with the flow
description: Plan every line from raw input to useful output. Give each step its machine, power, ingredient buffer and collection point. Chapters I–X provide the recipes; this page helps make those recipes run continuously.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Test one batch before connecting a large farm or bulk storage buffer.

quests.title: Rotation, speed and stress
description: Create machinery needs a connected rotating network. Speed changes can also change stress requirements. Inspect the machine and network feedback before adding more equipment or gearing up.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: When a line stalls, check the output, rotation and stress status before rebuilding the recipe.

quests.title: Build the assembly in order
description: T&K3 mechanisms use one-loop sequenced assembly. Put the base onto a belt or depot and carry it through the operations in the recipe’s exact order. The Kinetic Mechanism starts from a wooden slab, receives Andesite Alloy twice and finishes under an iron hammer.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: A wrong ingredient or skipped operation leaves an incomplete item instead of a finished mechanism.
steps: Stock each operation from a labelled buffer.
Place the listed finishing tool in the last Deployer.
Run one complete item and inspect the finished output.

quests.title: Tools need a supply plan
description: Ordinary finishing tools wear during assembly. Chapter rewards replace that maintenance with a named unbreakable version per player. Until then, keep an accessible replacement buffer and inspect the final Deployer when production stops.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Keep combat tools out of the automatic ingredient feed.

quests.title: Deploy the mechanism onto its casing
description: A machine frame is assembled by deploying its mechanism onto the matching casing. Functional machines combine a frame with matching mechanical parts. Stonecutting remains useful for the listed passive fittings; every choice consumes its frame.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Only the first Kinetic Machine has the expensive raw-material startup shortcut.
steps: Follow the machine’s exact recipe: frame plus working parts. Use stonecutting only for listed passive fittings.

quests.title: Renewable stone and elements
description: Build a water/lava cobblestone or stone generator. Place the selector directly below the newly generated block and its correct frame one block below the selector. The custom generator changes the new stone into the selected geological block.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: A missing selector or wrong frame gives the ordinary generator result. Obsidian remains obsidian.
steps: Choose a row from the wiki’s generator table.
Place selector and frame in the two blocks below the generation position.
Run the generator and collect its output.
Mill the early material or crush it once Chapter III is available.

quests.title: Give each stone a destination
description: Andesite supplies clay, Diorite quartz, Granite lapis and Limestone bone meal. Veridium supplies copper and Crimsite iron. In Brass, Scoria supplies redstone, Scorchia coal, Asurine zinc and Ochrum gold. Milling and crushing have their own listed yields.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Keep the generator’s raw output apart from processed dusts and metals. Crushing Wheels start in Chapter III.

quests.title: A renewable wood line
description: A Create tree farm needs harvesting, sapling supply, replanting and output transfer. Plan each job before scaling the contraption. Supported wood processing cuts logs into stripped logs, then six planks.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep a protected sapling reserve so downstream crafting cannot eat the next planting batch.
steps: Test the selected tree type on a small area.
Transfer the harvest into a wood buffer.
Send only the needed logs into processing.

quests.title: Wheat and kelp become slime
description: The authored mixer route uses one wheat, one kelp and 250 mB water to produce two slimeballs. Slime and dried kelp then feed Rubber Compound, making the early sealing line renewable.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Pump water into a dedicated buffer and keep surplus wheat available for food.

quests.title: Fans and processing conditions
description: Washing, haunting and other fan processes depend on the correct fan setup and recipe. Use JEI and Ponder to check the required medium and placement. Do not assume every crushed item has a washing result.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Filter the output and test one item before attaching the entire ore store.

quests.title: Slice & Dice in the kitchen
description: The Slicer automates supported Farmer’s Delight cutting recipes with the appropriate held knife. The Sprinkler belongs to the field-and-fluid tier. Inspect the actual supported cutting recipe and water arrangement before scaling.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Put a knife replacement plan next to the kitchen ingredients.

quests.title: Storage on a contraption
description: The selected Sophisticated integrations connect storage and backpacks to Create systems. Test the supported inventory on a small contraption and confirm which upgrades and transfers work there.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Verify that cargo leaves the moving inventory before extending the farm.

quests.title: Liquid experience and enchantments
description: Enchantment Industry gives experience-processing equipment and its native enchanting rules. Use the Chapter V routes, keep XP apart from water and other fluids, and check the selected recipe for the desired operation.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: A liquid XP supply does not make every enchantment free or remove native requirements.

quests.title: Buffers before clever logistics
description: Use small input buffers, exact filters and a visible overflow plan. Brass-tier logistics can supply requested ingredients, but they still need available stock and working transfers.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: A buffer near the machine makes it easier to see whether the failure is production or transport.

quests.title: Run a useful line unattended
description: Choose one renewable workshop material. Connect resource production, processing and storage, then let several complete batches run without hand-feeding ingredients.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Inspect the line again when the output buffer is nearly full.
steps: Choose an alloy, mechanism, crop or wood line.
Test repeated batches and output collection.

guide_chapters.title: Power & Digital Logistics
guide_chapters.subtitle: Chapter IV onward · Mekanism, AE2 and Applied Mekanistics

quests.title: Three systems, three jobs
description: Create rotation runs the mechanical workshop. FE powers electric machinery. AE2 stores items and coordinates crafting. Mekanism chemicals add another material layer; a power cable is not a chemical pipe.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Build a small working example of each connection before combining them.

quests.title: Start electric power with precision
description: Chapter IV begins with heated steel, Steel Casing and Precision Mechanisms. These bootstrap powered processing, a Heat Generator, basic cables, the AE2 Charger and Inscriber before the Inductive Machine exists.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Follow Chapter IV’s order to avoid planning a machine that needs the component it is supposed to produce.

quests.title: Configure inputs and outputs
description: Mekanism machines have side and transfer settings. Give energy, items and chemicals the appropriate connections, then verify a single operation. Upgrading a machine is not a substitute for configuring it.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: If the recipe is correct but no progress starts, inspect the machine’s energy and side screens.

quests.title: Your first ME network
description: Begin with power input, a terminal, a drive and a small storage cell. Add automation only after you can insert and retrieve materials reliably. The native network’s energy and channel rules still apply.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep frequently used ingredients in the network and a small recovery reserve outside it.

quests.title: Teach a process, then request it
description: Autocrafting needs a valid pattern, a supported execution device and somewhere for the result to return. Distinguish a crafting pattern from a processing recipe that runs in an external machine.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Test a single requested batch with empty machine inputs before building many parallel interfaces.

quests.title: Upgrades preserve what matters
description: The managed storage and factory upgrades retain their native component-preserving recipe behavior. Use the supported upgrade route to keep stored contents and configuration rather than substituting an arbitrary shaped recipe.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Make a backup before testing major inventory upgrades on your main world.

quests.title: Chemical storage is its own layer
description: Applied Mekanistics adds chemical network storage alongside AE2. Chapter VI introduces the managed chemical housing and native preserving cell upgrades. Use compatible chemical storage and transfers rather than putting a gas into an item cell.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep each chemical line labelled. Hydrogen, chlorine and hydrogen chloride have different jobs.

quests.title: Feed only what a machine needs
description: Keep background production and on-demand production distinct. A permanent supply line can fill a buffer; a request-based line should return precisely the expected result to the network.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Reserve some basic materials so a request does not consume all of your startup stock.

quests.title: A remote factory still needs service
description: Wireless and quantum links help with remote storage access, but their native energy, range, channel and linking rules remain. Remote machines also need working world loading under your instance’s settings.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Test insertion, retrieval and production while you are away from the workshop.

guide_chapters.title: Routes, Rails & Airships
guide_chapters.subtitle: A connected kingdom · Brass transport and Integrated expeditions

quests.title: Choose the route for the job
description: Roads, Create transport, Hypertubes, Waystones and Aeronautics serve different kinds of travel and cargo. Plan stations and delivery inventories before adding long routes.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Start with a short route between two known inventories or safe landing points.

quests.title: Test a short Hypertube route
description: Chapter III supplies precision-based entrances and accelerators alongside native tube sections. Build a short accessible route, supply its required power and test both ends before extending it.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Leave room around entrances so you can service the route.

quests.title: Give a route a useful cargo job
description: Use Create’s supported transport components and Ponder to plan track, stations and cargo handling. Tie each destination to a real buffer, such as crop delivery or timber collection.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Confirm unloading before adding another stop.

quests.title: Supply the colony through the workshop
description: Create: MineColonies Link is selected to connect workshop logistics with colony requests. Inspect the installed link’s supported blocks and in-game guidance, then test one requested material with a small supply.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Give the colony a dedicated buffer so settlement demand does not consume the entire mechanism line.

quests.title: Build the first expedition vessel
description: Chapter VII introduces Expedition Frames for Aeronautics controls. Plan a light hull, balanced propulsion, steering, fuel or power, and cargo access. Follow the addon’s actual supported setup.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Test turning, stopping and cargo access close to home before crossing a long distance.

quests.title: Power and processing aboard
description: Aeronautics Mekanism compatibility provides the selected moving-vessel integration. Check which blocks and networks are supported in the installed versions, then test one electric machine aboard before expanding.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Observe power, inputs and outputs during movement as well as while parked.

quests.title: Travel and magic aboard
description: The current selection includes Aeronautics integrations for FTB Chunks, Iron’s Spells and Waystones: Sable. Read each installed addon’s supported behavior and settings before relying on claims, spell effects or travel from a moving vessel.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Test the exact interaction on a short trip with a safe landing point.

quests.title: Build a resupply outpost
description: Make a remote stop with fuel or energy, food, storage and repair supplies. Record the approach route and a safe landing area so the next expedition starts prepared.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Leave an emergency return option for the crew.

guide_chapters.title: Ars Nouveau · The Living Workshop
guide_chapters.subtitle: Spells, Source and magical automation alongside the factory

quests.title: Learn Ars on its own terms
description: Ars Nouveau combines a spellbook, glyphs, Source and automation devices. Use its in-game guide and JEI together. Your class’s Iron’s spell attributes do not automatically describe every Ars spell or Source device.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Start with one useful spell and one reliable Source supply.

quests.title: A first spellbook
description: Follow the native spellbook recipe and upgrade requirements shown in JEI. Read the guide’s instructions for making and editing a spell, then test a simple combination in a safe area.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep spell testing away from crops, settlers and important machine rooms.

quests.title: Read glyphs before combining them
description: Glyphs describe how a spell starts, what it does and how it is modified. Inspect the available glyphs and their costs before building a complicated sequence.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: A short spell whose effects you understand is easier to improve.

quests.title: Source is a production supply
description: Sourcelinks generate Source under their own conditions and jars hold it for supported devices. The Chapter IV Agronomic Sourcelink bootstrap uses wheat, Source Gems, a Source Jar and a Precision Machine.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Keep Source generation close enough to the actual consumers under Ars’s native transfer rules.

quests.title: A parallel arcane workshop
description: A Precision Machine bootstraps the Enchanting Apparatus before the custom Arcane Machine. Produce Arcane Casing and its sequenced mechanism, then deploy the mechanism onto the casing. This is a supporting branch alongside electric industry.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: The Arcane Machine is not a prerequisite for starting the first Source supply.

quests.title: Helpers with clear jobs
description: Ars automation helpers each have their own binding and task rules. Give a helper one supported job and a visible destination, then test collection before adding more work.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep the output inventory accessible so you can see whether the helper is collecting or stalled.

quests.title: Ars Creo · Starbuncle Wheel
description: Ars Creo’s Starbuncle Wheel adds a real Ars/Create connection. Follow its native operating rules and Ponder or in-game guide, then test it on a small rotating setup.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Check the wheel’s actual operating conditions instead of treating Source as a universal replacement for every power system.

quests.title: Create and Source together
description: Create: Ars Nouveau compatibility and Wizardry are selected workshop integrations. Inspect each actual recipe and machine tooltip to see whether the process needs rotation, Source, a spell or more than one system.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Label Source connections separately from water, liquid XP and other fluid lines.

quests.title: Magical equipment and relics
description: Reliquified Ars Nouveau and Ars ’n Spells extend selected equipment or compatibility systems. Read the item’s own effects and restrictions; an Ars item and an Iron’s spellbook still have distinct rules.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Test one supported effect at a time when comparing a hybrid loadout.

quests.title: A living supply line
description: Build one Ars-assisted crop, collection or processing setup whose output feeds the workshop or storehouse. Include Source supply, the helper or device and a collection buffer.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep manual access to the buffer so the team can service the line.

guide_chapters.title: Iron’s Spells · The Spellcraft Hall
guide_chapters.subtitle: Schools, mana, scrolls, jewelry and selected spell addons

quests.title: Build a useful spell loadout
description: Iron’s Spells ’n Spellbooks uses its own spells, schools, mana and equipment. Start with a damage option and a utility or recovery option, then compare their costs and cooldowns.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Your spell’s actual school matters more than the visual color of its effect.

quests.title: Learn the scroll and book rules
description: Use found or crafted scrolls and the supported spellbook stations according to their native requirements. Inspect rarity, level, slots and prerequisites before committing a valuable scroll.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep a record of the spells you already use so you do not replace a useful utility spell by accident.

quests.title: Mana, casting time and cooldown
description: Mana capacity, regeneration, casting time and cooldown are different limits. A bigger mana pool does not guarantee faster recovery between fights. Read your gear and skill node effects together.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Test several casts in succession and watch what becomes the bottleneck.

quests.title: Specialize by school
description: The current classes support Holy, Blood, Ender, Eldritch, Fire, Ice and Lightning themes in different ways. Read a spell’s tooltip to confirm that it belongs to the school you are building around.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: The relevant attribute must exist in the installed mod version for a school-specific bonus to apply.

quests.title: Brewing and spell supplies
description: The selected Iron’s KubeJS bridge manages supported cauldron recipes while native spell systems remain. Inspect the exact recipe and fluid requirement in JEI before building a potion or reagent supply.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep brewing inputs and finished bottles in separate storage.

quests.title: The Jewelcrafting Guide
description: Iron’s Gems ’n Jewelry keeps its native jewel and component systems. Chapter II supplies the station and guide. Read the actual jewel and component effects before assembling equipment for your class.
quests.goal: Obtain and read the Jewelcrafting Guide.
tips: Use the station recipe and guide together; a jewel’s effect depends on the resulting equipment.

quests.title: Spells found through adventure
description: Alex’s Caves: Spellbooks, Cataclysm: Spellbooks and Twilight Forest: Spellbooks connect magic to their corresponding adventures. Inspect the installed addon’s JEI entries and discovery rules, then choose one spell to pursue.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Let your current workshop access and combat readiness guide the destination.

quests.title: Expanded spell schools and effects
description: Geomancy Plus, Archaion: Echoes of the Fallen and Echoing Magic: Esoteric Spells of the Fallen are selected spell additions. Read each spell’s real school, acquisition route and effect. The questbook does not invent an unlock item for these native spells.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Compare new spells in the training yard before relying on them during a boss fight.

quests.title: Match spellcraft to a class
description: Mage favors sustained or elemental casting, Cleric favors Holy and recovery themes, and Occultist favors Blood, summons or void schools. Rogue and Warrior hybrid paths can support specific effects without making every spell a melee bonus.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Read the class and subclass root penalties before choosing your final equipment.

quests.title: A complete spellcraft trial
description: Equip your chosen book and accessories, test a damage spell and a utility or recovery spell, then finish an ordinary expedition without exhausting your supply plan.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Bring normal food and equipment too; spells are part of the loadout.

guide_chapters.title: Witchery · The Hedge Scholar
guide_chapters.subtitle: Just Another Witchery Remake · native discovery and a careful study journal

quests.title: A different magical tradition
description: Just Another Witchery Remake is in the current alpha mod selection. Its magic is a separate branch from Ars Source and Iron’s spellbooks. Use the installed mod’s guide entries and JEI to discover the available systems.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Keep a dedicated study journal for recipes and prerequisites you have actually found.

quests.title: Find the first native guide
description: Inspect the installed Witchery entries and locate the guide or starter information available in this release. Record one verified starting recipe and its ingredients.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Addon versions can differ, so follow the guide in your instance.

quests.title: The hedge garden
description: Choose a plant or reagent that the installed Witchery recipes use, identify its actual source and grow or gather a renewable supply where the native rules allow it.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Protect a planting reserve before sending herbs into crafting.

quests.title: A separate ritual workspace
description: Set aside an accessible area for the native workstations or ritual setups you discover. Follow their actual placement and environment requirements rather than substituting a Create basin or Ars apparatus.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Leave space to expand without moving the whole workshop.

quests.title: Document one working process
description: Choose a native Witchery process, complete its prerequisites and run it. Write down the input, required setup and result so another player can reproduce it.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Confirm the result before reserving large quantities of a rare reagent.

quests.title: A hedge scholar’s contribution
description: Find one native Witchery result that is useful to your own adventures or settlement. Prepare its materials, demonstrate the result and add it to the town library’s notes.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: The activity check records the project; it does not add a custom transformation or ritual unlock.

guide_chapters.title: The Explorer’s Journal
guide_chapters.subtitle: Worlds, structures, travel and a safe return

quests.title: Explore with a purpose
description: Choose a destination for a useful discovery: crop, building palette, spell, equipment or workshop ingredient. Bring supplies, inventory space and a plan for returning home.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Record discoveries you cannot use yet; they may become useful in a later tier.

quests.title: A world of building palettes
description: Biomes O’ Plenty, Oh The Biomes We’ve Gone, Atmospheric, Environmental, Autumnity and other selected world mods add places and materials to explore. Bring home a palette sample and note its location.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Check whether a plant can be grown at home before committing to a long repeat trip.

quests.title: Discover a new structure
description: Integrated structures, YUNG’s improvements and the selected dungeon additions create exploration destinations. Approach carefully, identify an exit and distinguish ordinary loot from a boss objective.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Mark the entrance and unfinished rooms on your map.

quests.title: Looting as a team
description: Lootr is selected for supported personal-loot containers. Read the actual container feedback and server settings rather than assuming every chest in the world behaves the same.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Agree on rules for ordinary shared chests and expedition supplies.

quests.title: A useful travel stop
description: Waystones and the selected Better Party integrations support travel arrangements under their actual settings. Establish a safe stop and check activation, cost and party access before relying on it as the only return route.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Give destinations clear names that the whole team can recognize.

quests.title: The Brass expedition
description: Nether entry begins after Chapter II. Find the ingredients and Blaze access required by the Brass workshop, then record a safe return path. BetterNether and the selected Nether world changes provide further destinations.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Capture a Blaze in the appropriate burner when preparing heated brass production.

quests.title: Discover an Alex’s Cave
description: Alex’s Caves and its selected spell integration offer biome-specific discoveries. Follow their actual guide and discovery mechanics, identify the biome’s hazards and return with one useful finding.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Stock supplies for the conditions of the cave you are visiting.

quests.title: A bestiary entry
description: Alex’s Mobs, Mowzie’s Mobs, Ice & Fire and the selected encounter mods bring creatures with different behaviors. Observe one new creature, read available guidance and record how to approach or avoid it.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: An unfamiliar creature is not automatically safe because it looks peaceful.

quests.title: Bring the discovery home
description: Sort an expedition’s haul into food, building materials, gear, magic and progression supplies. Record where rare materials came from so the next trip has a clear purpose.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Leave room in the incoming-materials area before the team returns with full backpacks.

guide_chapters.title: The Boss Trial Ledger
guide_chapters.subtitle: Five permanent campaign catalysts · extra encounters stay optional

quests.title: Know which trial matters
description: The campaign uses Dragon Core, Verdant Sigil, Storm Core, Ember Core and Void Core. Their actual detected kill goals and rewards live in the matching Mechanical chapter. Other bosses remain optional adventures.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Use this ledger for preparation and the main chapter for the detected kill task.

quests.title: Chapter V · The Ender Dragon
description: Open the End through its native twelve-different-eyes requirement. The detected Dragon trial in Chapter V awards the permanent Dragon Core as a team reward.
quests.goal: Understand the trial and prepare for its main-chapter quest.
tips: Collect Dragon’s Breath while the fight gives you the opportunity; it supports later processing.

quests.title: Chapter VI · The Twilight Lich
description: Follow Twilight Forest’s native progression to the Lich. A player kill gives the reusable Verdant Sigil through the authored loot rule.
quests.goal: Understand the trial and prepare for its main-chapter quest.
tips: Clear the native earlier progression and read the boss’s defenses before starting the fight.

quests.title: Chapter VII · The Harbinger
description: Prepare for Cataclysm’s Harbinger encounter. A player kill gives the reusable Storm Core. Use the chapter’s detected trial to follow campaign progress.
quests.goal: Understand the trial and prepare for its main-chapter quest.
tips: Prepare your arena approach, recovery supplies and a clear way to retreat before engaging.

quests.title: Chapter VIII · Ignis
description: Prepare for the native Ignis encounter. A player kill gives the reusable Ember Core; it remains a catalyst for the final imprinting sequence.
quests.goal: Understand the trial and prepare for its main-chapter quest.
tips: Practice your current weapon and spells before entering the arena with valuable equipment.

quests.title: Chapter IX · The Ender Guardian
description: The Ender Guardian’s player-kill drop gives the permanent Void Core. The trial is available before the boss-gated Singularity Frame and supports Void-attuned Singularity production.
quests.goal: Understand the trial and prepare for its main-chapter quest.
tips: Do not plan the core’s first acquisition around equipment that already needs that core.

quests.title: Keep the cores, repeat the production
description: Core-bearing deployment steps retain their core. The final Sovereign Keystone imprints all five onto a Sovereign Core and finishes with the ordinary Enchanter’s Sword. Repeated boss kills can supply additional parallel catalyst stations.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Store cores in a labelled secure inventory and keep them out of void or disposal upgrades.

quests.title: Extra bosses and discoveries
description: Bosses’ Rise, Mowzie’s Mobs, Ice & Fire, Cataclysm and selected structure addons offer more encounters than the five mandatory campaign catalysts. Choose one suitable encounter and document its native reward.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Optional encounters do not award invented campaign cores.

guide_chapters.title: Into the Twilight Forest
guide_chapters.subtitle: Native adventure order · Lich catalyst from Chapter VI

quests.title: Follow the forest’s own progression
description: Twilight Forest has its own entry and boss progression. Use the native guide, advancements and in-world clues to understand the next destination. The campaign’s Verdant Sigil comes from the Lich player kill.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: A workshop tier does not skip the forest’s earlier native progression requirements.

quests.title: Prepare the forest journey
description: Read the installed portal requirements, bring food and a return plan, and mark your entry location. Leave space for discoveries instead of bringing every workshop tool.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep a spare recovery kit on the home side of the portal.

quests.title: Your first forest objective
description: Complete an early native forest objective and read the advancement or guide that explains the next one. Record a route and useful materials for a return visit.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Use native progression feedback when a biome or boss is inaccessible.

quests.title: Prepare for the Lich trial
description: Complete the forest’s preceding requirements, find the Lich destination and review your loadout. Chapter VI contains the campaign kill task; its authored player-kill loot gives the Verdant Sigil.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Take a reliable ranged or spell option if your chosen approach needs one.

quests.title: Forest relics and spellbooks
description: The selected Reliquified Twilight Forest and Twilight Forest: Spellbooks integrations add their own discoveries. Inspect what you actually find and follow each item’s native upgrade or acquisition rules.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep promising equipment even if it suits another teammate’s class better.

quests.title: A reusable forest route
description: Record entry, cleared objectives, useful materials and an unfinished destination in the town library. Bring home enough supplies to make the next trip a planned expedition.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Separate progression trophies and crafting supplies when sorting the haul.

guide_chapters.title: Beyond the End Portal
guide_chapters.subtitle: Chapter V · unique eyes, the Dragon and renewable End materials

quests.title: Prepare before crossing
description: The End opens after Chapter IV. End Remastered still requires twelve different valid eyes. Four eyes have authored Inductive Mechanism deployment routes; other unique eyes retain their native discovery sources.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Keep a list of distinct eye types instead of collecting twelve copies of the same one.

quests.title: Twelve different eyes
description: Inspect the four managed eye deployments in Chapter V and gather the remaining valid types through exploration. Check the portal’s native acceptance rules before committing your collection.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Build several exploration goals around eye types you are still missing.

quests.title: The first Dragon expedition
description: Prepare blocks, food, equipment, free bottle space and a return plan. Follow the detected Chapter V Dragon trial and manually claim its Dragon Core reward after the kill is recorded.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Keep the core for production; the first core comes from the quest reward rather than a guessed Dragon loot recipe.

quests.title: Bring back Dragon’s Breath
description: Collect Dragon’s Breath during the fight. Create: Dragons Plus uses its native breath filling, emptying and ending fan processes, with the managed fluid hatch supporting transport.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep empty bottles ready before the fight and sort the collected breath into its own supply.

quests.title: Grow the End at home
description: Bring chorus supplies and End Stone home, then build a repeatable growing and harvest area. Chorus supports the Ender and chemical workshop layers.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Reserve planting stock before feeding chorus to industrial processing.

quests.title: Explore the End’s new palette
description: BetterEnd: New Dawn, Nullscape and the selected End changes provide destinations and materials beyond the first island. Plan travel, record routes and bring home a building or crafting discovery.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep a dependable return option before extending a remote exploration route.

guide_chapters.title: Oceans & Aquatic Workshops
guide_chapters.subtitle: Copper tier · Upgrade Aquatic and Create: Aquatic Ambitions

quests.title: An ocean worth exploring
description: Upgrade Aquatic supplies selected aquatic world content. Create: Aquatic Ambitions connects ocean materials to the workshop. Bring breathing and travel supplies appropriate to the actual destination.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Start with a nearby coast and record useful ocean locations.

quests.title: Calcium-Rich Powder
description: The managed mixing route uses bone meal, kelp and water. Keep these inputs available for Prismarine Alloy production and follow the Chapter II metallurgy chain.
quests.goal: Produce Calcium-Rich Powder for the aquatic metallurgy line.
tips: Limestone milling can support the bone-meal buffer.

quests.title: Prismarine Alloy
description: Compact prismarine shard, copper sheet and calcium powder into the managed alloy. Continue through the listed rods and Conduit Cage components rather than assuming every aquatic block shares a vanilla recipe.
quests.goal: Produce the aquatic workshop alloy.
tips: Reserve ocean materials for the first cage before spending them on decorations.

quests.title: Read the real channeling process
description: Build the managed Conduit Cage and use Aquatic Ambitions’ actual channeling recipes. Its conduit ingredient comes from ocean exploration; the alloy route does not remove that exploration step.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Use the recipe tab to check each channeling operation’s real requirements.

quests.title: A coastal supply station
description: Build a safe coastal store with fishing supplies, spare food and space for kelp and ocean materials. Connect a useful resource to the town storehouse.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep a few exploration supplies in the station for the next trip.

guide_chapters.title: Fields, Food & the Kitchen
guide_chapters.subtitle: Farmer’s Delight, Slice & Dice and the selected Let’s Do cooking mods

quests.title: Food and industry share the fields
description: Your crops can feed players, colony workers and the factory. Wheat and kelp support slime and seals; later crop processing supplies Bio Fuel. Plan separate food, planting and industrial buffers.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: A factory should receive the surplus, not consume the farm’s last planting materials.

quests.title: A farm with a clear job
description: Choose a crop your team uses and build a small farm with access to water, collection and a planting reserve. Check the crop’s actual growing rules and available harvesting methods.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Make each field’s destination visible with a sign or labelled chest.

quests.title: The useful kelp patch
description: Kelp feeds Algal Blend, the slime route and aquatic calcium production. Build collection first and keep the factory’s intake separate from a spare growing area.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: The manual blend route starts your workshop; mixing improves its yield later.

quests.title: A proper cutting station
description: Farmer’s Delight cutting recipes use their listed tool and output rules. Start with the native board, inspect recipes in JEI and later automate supported cuts with Slice & Dice.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep ingredients and the cutting tool nearby so manual food prep remains easy.

quests.title: The Stove
description: Use Farmer’s Delight’s native cooking setup and recipes to prepare repeatable meals. Plan the input supply and finished-meal storage before adding automatic transfers.
quests.goal: Obtain a Stove and prepare a place for the kitchen.
tips: Choose a meal whose ingredients are already renewable in your settlement.

quests.title: More kitchens, more choices
description: Farm & Charm, Bakery, Brewery, Candlelight and BloomingNature add selected farming, food or decoration content. Inspect each mod’s actual recipe stations rather than treating every dish as a Farmer’s Delight pot recipe.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Pick one useful recipe from each system you want to build, instead of stocking every ingredient at once.

quests.title: Keep animal feed in reserve
description: Plan shelter, breeding supplies and collection around the animals you actually keep. Store animal feed apart from the crop input that the factory consumes.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Leave safe access for manual care even if parts of the collection become automatic.

quests.title: The Copper irrigation project
description: Chapter II includes the frame-based Sprinkler and hydraulic machinery. Follow the installed Sprinkler’s water requirements, then test a small field before expanding.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Inspect water supply and collection when evaluating the field’s performance.

quests.title: A farm that feeds the sealing line
description: Connect wheat and kelp reserves to the water-fed mixer route: one wheat, one kelp and 250 mB water produce two slimeballs. Use the output for Rubber Compound and Copper-tier mechanisms.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Protect meal ingredients and replanting stock with separate buffers.

quests.title: Food surplus becomes feedstock
description: Chapter VI turns suitable farm output into Mekanism Bio Fuel and the native substrate/ethylene/HDPE chain. Use JEI to choose a supported crop input; keep food-grade output available for people too.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Begin with the Ender Machine bootstrap equipment before planning Chemical Machine upgrades.

quests.title: A kitchen the whole team can use
description: Build a repeatable meal line with ingredient storage, the proper cooking station and finished-food collection. Demonstrate several batches and stock the expedition locker.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Place a small manual prep area next to the automated line.

guide_chapters.title: Storage, Backpacks & Collection
guide_chapters.subtitle: Useful upgrades early · digital storage later

quests.title: Sort by what you do next
description: Use named storage for crops, stone, processed metals, mechanisms, tools and expedition loot. Sophisticated Storage and Backpacks add useful upgrades, while ME arrives with Chapter IV.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Keep an incoming-materials chest so explorers can unload before sorting.

quests.title: A Backpack
description: A backpack gives your expeditions a dedicated inventory and upgrade system. Inspect its upgrade slots and tier recipe before adding features.
quests.goal: Obtain a Backpack for supplies and discoveries.
tips: Leave a few empty slots for discoveries rather than filling every slot with emergency supplies.

quests.title: The Hopper Upgrade
description: A Hopper Upgrade transfers between adjacent inventories using its configuration. It is useful for early machine input and output handling; it does not replace a Pickup Upgrade’s dropped-item job.
quests.goal: Obtain and configure a Hopper Upgrade.
tips: Set filters and test the transfer direction with a small item stack.

quests.title: The Pickup Upgrade
description: Use the Pickup Upgrade for dropped-item collection under its actual range and filter rules. Check the correct storage or backpack variant instead of assuming every upgrade fits both.
quests.goal: Obtain a Backpack Pickup Upgrade and inspect its settings.
tips: Test with a few dropped items before relying on it for an entire farm.

quests.title: Keep the important things
description: Filter what goes into each buffer. Planting stock, tools, boss catalysts and finished mechanisms need different destinations from ordinary overflow.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep your core inventory out of automatic disposal and void-upgrade routes.

quests.title: Upgrade the stored inventory
description: Use the supported tier and upgrade recipes shown in JEI. The managed preserving recipes retain native inventory components; inspect the intended result before upgrading your main container.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Test an upgrade on a small spare container first.

quests.title: Storage that moves
description: The selected Sophisticated Create integrations support their corresponding contraption inventory features. Test one supported container and transfer arrangement before turning it into a full harvesting system.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Watch the inventory during movement and when unloading.

quests.title: Hand off to ME cleanly
description: When Chapter IV opens digital storage, decide which buffers remain local and what moves into ME. Local food, tools and recovery materials are still useful when the network is unavailable.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep a visible reserve for the equipment that restores power or storage access.

guide_chapters.title: Build Your Colony
guide_chapters.subtitle: MineColonies, TownTalk and a factory that supplies the settlement

quests.title: Choose space for a real town
description: MineColonies has its own building, worker and research progression. Plan a location with room for buildings, roads and later expansion; inspect the native colony guide before placing the first layout.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Preview buildings and routes before filling the area with machines.

quests.title: The settlement supply plan
description: Prepare the native starting supplies shown in JEI and the colony guide. Keep the first builder’s requested materials in a dedicated buffer so workshop crafting cannot take them unexpectedly.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Choose a building style whose materials you can gather reliably.

quests.title: The Builder’s Hut
description: A builder manages native construction work through its hut and request system. Read the current request and provide the needed materials rather than repeatedly placing new unfinished projects.
quests.goal: Obtain a Builder’s Hut and plan its placement.
tips: Complete a small first build to learn the colony workflow.

quests.title: Homes, food and work
description: A settlement needs housing, food access and suitable jobs according to MineColonies’ native requirements. Grow one manageable neighborhood before creating demand across a huge unfinished town.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Use the colony screens to check what the citizens actually need.

quests.title: A readable warehouse
description: Plan deliveries and central storage around the colony’s supported warehouse and worker systems. Label the workshop’s supply buffer and avoid sending every rare material to general settlement storage.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Reserve factory catalysts and future-tier materials in a separate secure area.

quests.title: Follow the colony’s research
description: MineColonies research and building upgrades have their own native conditions. Read the requirement in the colony UI and pursue the next useful service rather than assuming a workshop milestone unlocks it automatically.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Choose a research goal that solves a current shortage.

quests.title: Connect one Create supply
description: Create: MineColonies Link supports the selected workshop integration. Follow the installed link’s guidance and test one colony material request from a dedicated Create supply.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Record where the request enters and where delivery finishes before expanding.

quests.title: Make the town feel inhabited
description: TownTalk and the selected colony integrations add character to settlement life. Explore the supported interactions and keep paths, service areas and citizen access clear.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Design plazas and practical service routes together rather than decorating over the traffic paths.

quests.title: A town ready for trouble
description: Follow the native colony’s guard and defense requirements, secure supply access and leave clear routes through the settlement. Test your own combat away from fragile colony work areas.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep a shared recovery kit and food reserve accessible.

quests.title: A working kingdom district
description: Finish a district with housing, a useful service, food access and a supplied construction or delivery route. Add signs so a new teammate can understand the town’s organization.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: A smaller finished district is easier to maintain and expand.

guide_chapters.title: Builders & Practical Details
guide_chapters.subtitle: Chipped, Architect’s Palette, Supplementaries and Amendments

quests.title: A building with a clear purpose
description: Give each building a job, a palette and room for access. Separate noisy processing, storage, food and magical experiments, then connect them with readable paths.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Use a limited palette with one accent material so the workshop remains easy to navigate.

quests.title: The Carpenter’s Table
description: Chipped workbenches turn supported materials into decorative variants. Inspect which workbench handles your chosen palette and keep these choices distinct from progression frames.
quests.goal: Obtain a Carpenter’s Table and inspect its decorative options.
tips: Test a wall section before producing the entire building palette.

quests.title: Architect’s Palette in the workshop
description: Architect’s Palette provides building materials and the Algal Blend used by the early industrial route. Decorative variants do not replace the required mechanism or frame in a machine recipe.
quests.goal: Understand this part of your adventure.
tips: Reserve enough kelp and clay for progression before committing them to a large build.

quests.title: Details that help people
description: Supplementaries and Amendments add practical building and interaction details. Choose actual supported items for signs, lighting, displays or useful room functions by reading their tooltips and recipes.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: A clear label beside an ingredient buffer is a useful part of the build.

quests.title: Design for maintenance
description: Leave room to reach machine faces, filters, tanks and tool-holding deployers. Add walkways through a factory so expanding a line does not cut off the rest of the building.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Plan vertical access before stacking a second processing floor.

quests.title: Finish a readable workshop room
description: Build a room with a consistent palette, visible storage labels, a clear machine flow and safe access to every important input and output.
quests.goal: Complete the project described below.
tips: Keep the raw-input end and finished-output end recognizable at a glance.
